questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
it was important for me that the country was in visiting distance from Denmark, so my friends, family and girlfriend to come see me. 
The options courseswise were a big factor aswwell.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it is hard to reach a 10. I wouldn't even score my normal day life a 10, so their will always be some sort of negative experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, Their were alot of people designated to information the first couple of weeks of arrivial.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In the intro week they have arranged a lot of different activities and assigned everybody to a group which you could use to get to know new people at these activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a complete nightmare to get a place, and the Amsterdam housemarket is a jungle. My advice is to start as early as possible and be flexible which how much you are willing to pay. The prices are quite high

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can have the feeling that you are kind of excluded from everyone. A lot of stuff is happning at campus, and sometimes people dont want to leave, so you must work that extra hard to be part of the community

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was super unnecessarily complicated. First step were to find the courses i wanted to have. Then i had to fill out quite comprehensive application. If this application were accepted, then i was given the right to apply for the courses, but not guaranteed the courses. The applying for the courses came a couple months later, where you had to be ready for the release it is first come, first served, and the website crashed as soon as they opened op.
The easy part is , that Vrije universiteit creates theses "Minor courses" where the gather 5 courses about a specifik subject, which you can take over a semester

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Their were the exchange student office, which i could contact through mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got al the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look through the minor course list and see if there is one you find attractive. It will make it so much more easy to join one of them, instead of creating your own list of courses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I felt the level of courses was a bit below the standard of UCPH, but the exams were quite hard because they asked about stuff, that would be completely irrelevant to learn back home. Where we are learned to use and elborate the knowledge we retain, their might ask in an exam what year a theory was invented and by whom

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had only lectures i big classes. Their were no interaction between the student, and close to none with the lecturer themself

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction Psychology
Evolutionary Psychology
Behaviour Genetics in Psychology
Biological Psychology
Neuropsychology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction Psychology, because it was a super nice introduction course to the world of psychology and the lecturer was amazing
Behaviour Genetics in Psychology. Gene psychology was just and amazing new world to look at, and again the lecturer was super good to do his thing and to get the student involved

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: How expensive it is to meet new people. Everything you do to get to know each other costs money

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Fast food is so much more expensive that what we are used to in CPH, and also their cheese is weirdly expensive
Is it worth it to keep an eye out for sales in the different supermarkets, because their really made them worth your while

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Their was a really nice fitness center available to a student discount, at the accommodation campus. Their also had a lot of different classes you could take. Their were also a lot of different sports clubs, like row, karate and basket. Unfortunately for me they didn't have any sort of football clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: try the poledance class in the fitness center. It was so much fun and so different to what you might normally do

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just explore the city. Amsterdam have so many amazing areas, but for me it was more fun to discover them on my own, than to go somewhere others have told me about.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy, Amsterdam is pretty much just Copenhagen on steroids. So everything seems familiar but just a bit off

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: none at all. The local students doesn't really want to have anything to do with exchange student. So you friends will be other exchange student

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The trafik. Amsterdam have the worst trafik i have every experienced. They run a lot of red light, the bikes own the road and no one, i mean absolutely no one, gives any sort of signs, both cars and bikes

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nightlife. Once you go out you will meet some amazing people. Because Amsterdam is so multicultural you will engage in so many different new social encounters and the people are super friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Start on the house search as soon as you know you are going
2. Be okay with the fact that you are not gonna experience that many dutch people. Your social arena will be other exchange students
3. Relax about the academic level. I promise you, youøll do fine

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a routine going, so you'll have some sort of backbone through the week, but say yes to any invitation that might lead you astray for that day

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people. I have meet some amazing lovely friends, which means that their are so many contries i now have an excuse to visit

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on you own. There are no safety net to catch you on your bad days, and you will have super much time on your own. You'll have to learn to really be your own best friend

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just go do it. If you are thinking about it, then i promise you you'll be happy that you did it

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
